newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police follow Internet clue to beheading.
newsitem.headline: Japan police follow Internet clue to beheading.

text.p: Japanese police are following an Internet clue to last month's murder and beheading of an 11-year-old boy, officials said on Saturday.
They were investigating an Osaka Internet provider after messages similar to a note found in the Kobe schoolboy's mouth appeared on a home page, police said on Saturday.

An unidentified provider earlier this year displayed a message similar to the murder note, including the words "wine", "devil" and "rose" in red Chinese characters on a black background, Japan's Kyodo News Service reported.
A person claiming to be Jun Hase's killer wrote to the Kobe Shimbun newspaper on June 4 that the same Chinese characters, which read "Sakakibara", were his name.
The home page was closed to the public in May because of obscene messages, Kyodo quoted a company official as saying.

Jun left his home in Kobe on May 24, saying he was going to visit his grandfather. Three days later the sixth-grader's severed head was found at the foot of the iron gate of a nearby junior high school.
His body was discovered in a forest near Tainohata Elementary School where he was a pupil.
The author of the murder note described himself as an "invisible man" with "no nationality" and said he enjoyed killing and would strike again, police said.
